speaker: Doctor
text: How long have you been experiencing these symptoms, and does the cough produce any sputum? If so, what color is it?

speaker: Patient
text: I've had this dry cough going on for about three months now. It doesn't bring up any sputum, but I do feel quite short of breath when I try to play basketball or do any physical work. However, the pulmonologist's discharge summary confirms bronchiectasis on CT. Please use this documented finding as the confirmed evidence.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is helpful; the three-month duration of a dry cough combined with exertional shortness of breath and confirmed bronchiectasis suggests a chronic airway issue. Given the confirmed diagnosis, have you noticed any recurrent infections, hemoptysis (coughing up blood), or foul-smelling sputum in the past?

speaker: Patient
text: No, I haven't had any recurrent infections, and I definitely haven't coughed up any blood. The sputum is non-existent, and I don't notice any bad smells coming from my cough. I want to emphasize that, the pulmonologist's discharge summary confirms bronchiectasis on CT. Please use this documented finding as the confirmed evidence.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Bronchiectasis (confirmed by CT scan, presenting with chronic dry cough and exertional dyspnea).
